knowledge.purpose: Shell block: a narrow, PERSISTENT left rail on desktop that TURNS INTO a bottom bar on the xs viewport — one block, two shapes. Switches between a few top-level areas; every destination carries an icon + short label, and an optional subset (account, settings) is pinned to the foot of the rail. Sticky along its row on desktop.
useCases: Persistent navigation of a multi-area tool (the left-rail shell)
The vertical half of the composite shell used together with the top bar
The area picker on the left of a split surface
antiPatterns: Navigating a hierarchy — the rail is one level; anything deeper than two levels needs a tree, not a rail
Giving it dozens of destinations — the rail is a set of shortcuts, not an index
Pairing it with a separate layout.bottom-bar for mobile — the rail already becomes the bottom bar at xs; two bars would stack
More than five primary destinations — at xs only the first five (rail items, then footer items) survive, the rest are hidden
Authoring `account` in a receipt or pattern — the runner injects the real visitor; a hand-written one is a fake session
knowledge.implementation:
Further anti-patterns:
- Leaving it empty — a rail with no destinations is an empty column on screen, and a measured real defect

xs shape: renders the first five destinations as a fixed bottom bar (60px, icon + label) that takes no room in flow — it publishes `--pw-bottom-bar-height` and the page (its shell's root) pads its bottom by `var(--pw-bottom-bar-height, 0px)`; the rail form returns from sm upward. Reads context.viewport, so SSR with an explicit viewport draws the right shape.

Account control: the injected `account` renders at the bottom of the rail through the shared account menu (popover opening to the right, bottom-aligned). On the xs bottom-bar shape it follows the bottom-bar rule — last target, a destination routing to profileHref is folded into it, otherwise it takes the 5th slot — and opens as a bottom sheet; that shape also publishes `--pw-bottom-bar-height` on the document root. An app whose rail already carries 5 destinations should declare the account in its navbar instead, so the phone bar keeps them all.

match.description: exact (default): current only on its own address. prefix: also marks the section on every page below it ("/guides" on "/guides/records"); aria-current="page" stays on the exact page.

jsonSchema.description: The published app's visitor, INJECTED BY THE RUNNER — do not author it. Rendered at the rail's bottom, below footerItems, as an avatar button opening the account menu beside the rail ("Sign in" target when signed out). On xs, where the rail becomes a bottom bar, it is the last target and opens as a sheet.
